question: How many species can a living Pokedex actually hold, and what does the current planner say?

defect.what: PokedexTarget answers 'what can one cartridge register', and its exclusion reasons say so explicitly. The multi-run planner inherited those exclusions unchanged, so four species marked REQUIRES_TRADE -- Alakazam, Machamp, Golem, Gengar -- were counted as unobtainable by any plan.
defect.why_it_is_wrong: Each is obtained by trading its precursor to a second live save, where it evolves on arrival, and trading it back. The obstacle was never the species. It was that nothing in the model could say a partner save exists.
defect.why_it_survived: Nothing distinguished a sequence of runs from a set of concurrent saves. On paper a three-run schedule and a three-vessel plan look the same, and only one of them can trade.

model: A campaign is concurrent vessels. A vessel is one save that exists at the same time as the others and can therefore trade. A trade-gated species is lifted only when the plan has at least two vessels AND some vessel can obtain the precursor -- trading requires something to send.

what_remains_at_three_red_saves.reading: Every one of the ten is obtainable in Blue. Adding a Blue vessel would leave only Mew, which no amount of cartridge planning reaches. So Gen 1's living Pokedex is 150/151 with four concurrent saves -- a number this project has never stated.

the_distinction_that_matters: Replaying a cartridge is not running two of them. Three sequential runs register 136 species across time and hold zero of them simultaneously, because the second save overwrites the first. Only concurrency produces a living collection, and 'must_trade_home' is the real cost of one: fifteen species have to be moved for three saves to become one collection.
next_concrete_step: No blue_target() exists, so the campaign model cannot yet be given a Blue vessel. Declaring Blue's target is a small, ROM-free change that would take the measured reach from 140 to 150.
self_correction: consolidation_required originally carried a has_trade_partner guard. Mutation testing showed no input could distinguish it -- a lone vessel's reach equals its own target by arithmetic -- so the test claiming to cover it was passing for the wrong reason. The guard was removed rather than kept untestable.

correction_2026_08_09.what_was_wrong: Every figure here counted ten version exclusives per cartridge. There are eleven. Scyther is Red's Game Corner exclusive and Pinsir is Blue's, and both were missing from the exclusion table these numbers were computed from.
correction_2026_08_09.how_it_was_caught: Two contracts in this repository disagreed about the one-save denominator -- the living-collection contract said 124 and the registration target said 125. That disagreement was noticed during an audit and dismissed as probably a difference of definition. It was not: it was this missing species, and chasing the discrepancy rather than rationalising it is what found it.
correction_2026_08_09.model_also_superseded: This record lifts a trade evolution when a plan has at least two vessels. That is now wrong too. Concurrency is necessary but not sufficient: two saves on incompatible titles or hardware coexist without being able to exchange anything, so a campaign now declares explicit TradeLink pairs and lifting requires one. The same three vessels with no links reach 146 rather than 150.
correction_2026_08_09.what_still_holds: Two Red plus one Blue still reaches 150 of 151 with Mew alone out of reach, and a third Red save still adds nothing once Blue is present. The headline survived the correction; the Red-only figures did not.
